_comment: The contact shape the agent console reads (GET /api/v1/contacts/{id}, the raw Contact entity, Verbara.Platform.Web src/core/api/hooks/use-contacts.ts) gains ONE computed member, `identityLevel`, derived from the contact's WebChat addresses with no stored column (design D10). Every other member keeps its name and meaning; null members stay ABSENT (WhenWritingNull). The console marks a contact from this member alone: `Unverified` -> "identity not verified" on the contact card, the conversation header and every row of the History tab; `Verified` -> a verified badge; `Anonymous` or absent -> no mark (design D11). Conversation shapes are UNCHANGED: every conversation of a contact shares its contact's level (no merge in this change, design D5), so ContactConversationSummaryDto of contact-history-opens-by-assignment (its fixtures/contact-conversation-history.v1.json) gains NO field and that change needs no follow-up for this one. The same section fixtures the refusal of a contact write that names a reserved WebChat identity key (design D12). Every child change's delta spec must cite these field names and codes VERBATIM (verbatim-fixture-citation rule, /xr:propagate).

addressForms.webchat-<32 lowercase hex>: a SESSION address: one per WebChat session, the reply destination of that session's conversation (unchanged form)
addressForms.webchat-visitor:<43 base64url chars>: the LEVEL-1 key: base64url, unpadded, of SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the normalised visitorId (lowercase, hyphenated). Identity only: never a reply destination, never shown raw anywhere because it is never stored raw
addressForms.webchat-external:<external_id>: the LEVEL-2 key: the verified token's external_id verbatim. Identity only: never a reply destination
addressForms._rule: all three are channel WebChat. The two `webchat-visitor:` / `webchat-external:` prefixes are RESERVED: only POST /webchat/sessions writes them. A WebChat address of either form typed through the contact routes before this change is renamed `legacy-<address>` by a one-shot data-only migration before the Api serves (design D14, round-1 audit F3): `legacy-webchat-external:x` is an ordinary address, reads Anonymous and is never found by a session. Every prefix test (reserved check, identityLevelRule, reply-destination skip) is ORDINAL and case-sensitive: `WebChat-External:x` is not a key, never reads Verified and is never found by a session (review P3, 2026-11-04). A contact keeps at most its 50 newest session addresses: a session create that would add a 51st drops the oldest (design D17)

identityLevelRule: else a WebChat address starting with `webchat-visitor:` -> "Unverified"
else a WebChat session address `webchat-<hex>` -> "Anonymous" (every contact created before this change, and every Anonymous session)
else (no WebChat address: a WhatsApp, Email, Voice... contact) -> absent

examples.case: level 1: a returning visitor known by browser only, two sessions so far
level 2: a customer the tenant's site signed for
Anonymous: a contact created before this change (or by a session with no usable visitorId)
a contact with no WebChat address: identityLevel is absent

contactWriteRefusals.case: POST /contacts names a reserved WebChat identity key
PUT /contacts/{id} names a reserved WebChat identity key; nothing is written

fields.identityLevel: string, `Verified` | `Unverified` | `Anonymous`, computed by identityLevelRule; ABSENT for a contact without any WebChat address. Read-only: POST/PUT /contacts ignore it in a body
fields.customFields.webchatEmail: string: the e-mail a WebChat session supplied (form field visitorEmail at level 1, token claim email at level 2), written only when the key is absent, by one targeted conditional update (never a full-row save; design D3). Display data: it never links contacts. It is matched by GET /contacts?search= so a GDPR export or purge can find the contact by e-mail (design D3)
fields.addresses: unchanged member; may now hold the reserved forms of addressForms, and at most 50 session addresses
